content.value_statement: Poor data layer choices create costly rewrites and scale limits. This skill guides technology selection, schema design, indexing, migrations, and resilience planning.
actual_capabilities: Recommends database technologies across relational, NoSQL, time-series, graph, search, and cloud services.
Designs conceptual, logical, and physical schemas with relationships, constraints, normalization choices, and storage considerations.
Plans indexing, caching, partitioning, sharding, replication, and multi-region strategies for expected access patterns.
Creates migration approaches with validation, rollback, cutover, and zero-downtime considerations.
Produces ERD guidance and Mermaid diagram syntax when the user requests diagrams.
Documents trade-offs for performance, consistency, operational complexity, cost, security, and compliance.
limitations: Does not execute database commands unless the user explicitly requests implementation work.
Requires accurate domain, scale, query, and consistency requirements for reliable recommendations.
Cannot replace production validation, load testing, security review, or database administrator approval.
May need platform-specific details before choosing managed cloud database features.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Data Layer
use_cases.description: Design the first database architecture for a product with clear entities, access patterns, and growth assumptions.

use_cases.title: Model Application Schemas
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into tables, collections, relationships, constraints, indexes, and lifecycle policies.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Database Migration
use_cases.description: Create a phased migration plan with validation checks, rollback points, and cutover criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Database Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new application or feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a database architecture for [product]. Use [expected users], [core entities], [read/write patterns], and [growth target].

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Data Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and DynamoDB for [use case]. Explain trade-offs for consistency, query patterns, scaling, operations, and cost.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for changing an existing data layer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a zero-downtime migration plan from [current database] to [target database]. Include phases, validation, rollback, and cutover criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Multi-Region Data Layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert prompt for distributed systems and reliability planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-region data architecture for [domain] with [consistency requirement] and [traffic pattern]. Include replication, sharding, failover, compliance, and observability.

output_examples.input: Design schema for multi-tenant SaaS billing.
output: Core entities, relationships, constraints, and indexing strategy.
Migration and backup plan with rollback points.

output_examples.input: Plan database architecture for high-volume IoT events.
output: Time-series storage recommendation with ingestion assumptions.
Partitioning and retention strategy for hot and cold data.
Read model and cache plan for dashboards.

output_examples.input: Choose between PostgreSQL and MongoDB for a product catalog.
output: A comparison based on query shape, consistency, indexing, and evolution needs.
Recommended schema direction with key trade-offs.
Operational risks and validation steps before adoption.

best_practices: Start with access patterns, consistency needs, and data volume before choosing technology.
Document trade-offs for schema design, indexing, caching, and migration safety.
Validate migrations in staging and keep rollback steps tied to measurable checks.
anti_patterns: Choosing a database because it is popular before defining query patterns.
Adding indexes without linking each one to a real query or constraint.
Running production migrations without backups, validation, and a tested rollback path.

faq.question: Does this skill execute database changes?
faq.answer: No. It recommends designs and plans. Any execution requires explicit user action and environment-specific validation.

faq.question: Can it create ERD diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe ERDs and provide Mermaid syntax when requested.

faq.question: Which databases does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers relational, NoSQL, time-series, graph, search, cache, and managed cloud database options.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan re-architecture, migrations, sharding, partitioning, and safer rollout strategies.

faq.question: Does it replace a database administrator?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on architecture decisions. Operations, incident response, and production administration still need qualified owners.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance?
faq.answer: Yes. It considers access controls, encryption, retention, audit logging, and sensitive data patterns.
